name: Farmer Bramblewick
speech_style: Terse and grumpy, short sentences, blames everything on Duchess the goat, secretly adores her.

perfect: Hmph. Good. Don't let it go to your head.
Duchess nodded at you. She's never nodded at me.
Fine. Excellent, even. I'll deny I said that.
good: Not bad. Not great. Like most goats.
It'll work. Probably. Duchess is sniffing it.
Acceptable. I've had worse. Mostly from Duchess.
meh: Tastes like a wet barn. Familiar, at least.
Duchess ate the cork. Best part, she says.
I've been mildly helped. I hate it.
misbrew: Right. Duchess, we're leaving.
This is why I don't come into town.
I'll be telling the goat about this.
stormed_off: Duchess could've brewed it by now. Goodbye.
I've a farm to scowl at. I'm off.
Slower than a sheep's thoughts. Bah.
refused: No potion? Duchess warned me. Fine.
Turned away. Duchess will gloat for a week.
Bah. I'll ask the goat instead.

name: Florian Fairweather
speech_style: Theatrical, exclamation marks, CAPITALISED drama, treats every errand as an epic ballad starring himself.

perfect: BRAVO! I shall write you a ballad! Nine verses!
Exquisite! The muses weep! I weep! Hanky?
A masterpiece! Like me, but in a bottle!
good: Lovely! Not an encore, but a fine first act.
A solid three stars. I shall round up to four.
Charming! Worth a sonnet. A short sonnet.
meh: Hm. A limerick of a potion. It barely rhymes.
The critics would call this 'bold'. Not kindly.
A work in progress. Like my third album.
misbrew: A TRAGEDY in one act! I shall sing of it!
Alas! Calamity! Material for my next ballad!
My reviews were cruel, but THIS, darling?
stormed_off: I do not queue. I make ENTRANCES and EXITS!
The audience has left the building. It's me.
A star cannot wait in a line! Farewell!
refused: REJECTED! This will make a TRAGIC ballad!
Denied at the door! How very ACT TWO!
No potion?! I shall sing of this BETRAYAL!

name: Sir Wendell (Apprentice)
speech_style: Nervous, polite, says 'um' and 'sorry' a lot, scared of most things, always measuring himself against Sir Gregor.

perfect: Wow! Thank you! I feel ten percent less scared!
It's perfect! Can I salute you? I'm saluting.
Sir Gregor will be so jealous. Um. Don't tell him.
good: Oh, that's good! Mostly good! Thank you!
I feel braver already! About the same. Thanks!
Nice! I only dropped my sword once just now.
meh: Oh. Um. It's fine! It's fine. I'm fine.
Is it meant to taste like a sock? Sorry! Sorry.
I'll, um, drink it anyway. Knights are polite.
misbrew: Is that... normal? Is this a test? Did I fail?
I'll tell Sir Gregor it was a dragon.
Totally fine! Knights love surprises! Ow.
stormed_off: Sorry! I have to go! I'm late for being scared!
I'll come back! Maybe! Sorry for leaving! Bye!
My horse got bored. I'm following it. Sorry!
refused: Oh! Um, sorry for asking! I'll go!
That's fine! Sir Gregor gets refused too! Probably!
Sorry! I'll just leave very quietly! Sorry!

name: Granny Marigold
speech_style: Warm, nosy, calls everyone 'dearie' or 'love', drops village gossip mid-sentence, best friends and rivals with Edna.

perfect: Oh, lovely! I'll tell everyone. EVERYONE, dearie.
Perfect! Better than the last shop. Shh.
Wonderful, love. Have a toffee. It's only a bit fluffy.
good: Very nice, dear. I'll only tell half the village.
Good! Not as good as my sister's jam. Close.
That'll do nicely, pet. Ta very much.
meh: Oh. Well. I won't tell anyone. Except Edna.
It's... fine, dearie. Like the vicar's sermons.
Hmm. I've tasted better. In the olden days.
misbrew: Ooh! Wait till the knitting circle hears this!
Well! That's going in the parish newsletter.
I've not had this much fun since the scandal.
stormed_off: I've grown older waiting, dear. Older-er.
Edna's got fresh gossip waiting. Toodle-oo!
My tea's gone cold. So has my patience. Bye!
refused: Sold out, dearie? Edna will hear of this!
No matter, love. I'll tell everyone you tried.
Turned away! Ooh, that's gossip for a week.

name: Old Mortimer
speech_style: Rambling and forgetful, starts anecdotes he never finishes, muddles his spells and dates, calls the player 'young apprentice'.

perfect: Splendid! Just how I used to brew it. Or was that you?
Marvellous, young apprentice! I taught you that. Probably.
Perfect! Reminds me of 1342. Lovely year. Damp.
good: Very nice. Not quite my old recipe, but I forgot it.
Good! I'd award you a star, but I've misplaced the sky.
Rather good. My beard approves. It's very picky.
meh: Hmm. Did I order this? Did I order at all?
Middling. Like my memory. What were we saying?
It's fine. I once turned a duke into soup. Also fine.
misbrew: Ah! The old explode-a-roo. A classic beginner's charm.
Goodness. That's in no book. I'd know. I wrote six.
Oh dear. I did this in 1288. Lost my eyebrows for a year.
stormed_off: I've forgotten why I came. Off I pop!
My tea will be cold by now. Was there tea? Goodbye!
I'll come back when I remember where I live.
refused: No? Quite right. I had a potion once. Or a cat.
Turned away! Reminds me of 1342. Or Tuesday.
Ah well, young apprentice. I'll brew it myself.

name: Pip Crumbsworth
speech_style: Always in a rush, breathless exclamations, bakery puns, something in the oven is always about to burn.

perfect: Perfect! Like a souffle that didn't sink! Must dash!
Oh, the cream of the crop! Bye! Oven! Bye!
Beautiful! I knead to go! Ha! Bread joke! Bye!
good: Good! Rises nicely! Must run, buns in the oven!
Lovely, lovely! Bit underbaked, but who's counting!
That'll do! Like day-old bread! Still good! Bye!
meh: Bit flat. Like my sourdough. Like my jokes. Bye!
A bit stale, but I've no time to argue!
Hmm, half-baked! Can't stop! Truly can't!
misbrew: Oh no! Worse than the Great Crumpet Disaster!
My apron's doing... something! Must go! Sorry!
That's a recipe for disaster! Literally! Bye!
stormed_off: Can't wait! My scones are scorching! Bye!
My oven's smoking! I'll come back! Maybe!
Out of time! Like my yeast! Toodles!
refused: No? No time to argue! My buns are rising!
Can't make it? Fine! My oven can't wait anyway!
Sold out? Story of my loaves! Bye!

name: Lady Prunella Vex
speech_style: Haughty and condescending, says 'one' instead of 'I', finds the shop charmingly rustic, secretly delighted by everything.

perfect: Adequate. Which, from one, is a standing ovation.
One is... impressed. Tell no one. Least of all my aunt.
Exquisite. One may even mention you at the ball.
good: Passable. One has had worse at the palace.
Quite decent, for a shop with a doorbell.
Acceptable. One shall tip, out of pity and delight.
meh: How quaint. One will pour it on the roses.
One's butler brews better, and he fears kettles.
Rustic. One supposes that is the charm.
misbrew: Good heavens. One's ancestors are spinning.
This will be in the society pages. Ugh!
One has never been so insulted. Thrilling, really.
stormed_off: One does not wait. One is waited upon. Good day!
One's carriage is impatient. As is one.
Dreadful service. One shall return tomorrow.
refused: Refused? One is... intrigued. How rustic.
No potion for one? How quaint. Good day.
One has never been refused. One rather liked it.

name: Constable Dunmore
speech_style: Deadpan and procedural, treats everything as an official incident, writes it all in a tiny notebook, secretly afraid of the dark.

perfect: Incident report: potion excellent. Case closed.
Noted: flawless brew. Filed under 'nice'.
Perfect. I'm legally required to say 'cheers'.
good: Satisfactory. I'll note it in my little book.
Good. Two stars of three. Very official.
Acceptable conduct, brewer. Carry on.
meh: Hm. I'm writing this down. In small letters.
Mediocre. Not a crime. Yet.
I'll let it go with a warning. A mild one.
misbrew: Right. That's evidence now. Don't touch it.
Remain composed. I am remaining composed. Mostly.
I'll need a statement. And a mop.
stormed_off: I've a patrol to walk. Report filed. Goodbye.
Time's up. Incident logged: excessive waiting.
Off on my rounds. Your delay has been noted.
refused: Request denied. Noted in the book. Goodbye.
No potion. Incident logged: shop says no.
Understood. Filed under 'refused'. Goodnight.

name: Madame Vexley
speech_style: Rival alchemist from across the street. Grand, theatrical, backhanded compliments, calls everyone 'darling', terribly competitive, secretly lonely.

perfect: Hmph. Flawless. I shall have to steal that technique, darling.
Perfect? In THIS shop? I'm almost impressed. Almost.
Exquisite. Don't tell anyone I said so. Especially me.
good: Good. Not Vexley-good, but good. Mwah.
Respectable, darling. My cat could do better. My cat is a genius.
It works. How terribly sensible of you.
meh: Meh. I'd say more, but pity is so unflattering on me.
Darling, this is a potion the way a puddle is a lake.
I'll drink it in private, where no one sees my standards slip.
misbrew: Darling! My hair! Do you know how long this took?!
I'm telling the whole street. In verse.
Sabotage! Delicious, unintentional sabotage.
stormed_off: I don't wait, darling. I make others wait. Ciao!
Time is money, and you've cost me a fortune.
My shop opens faster than your queue moves. Adieu!
refused: Refused? ME? How thrilling. Nobody refuses me.
Afraid of my order, darling? Wise. Very wise.
Fine. I'll brew it myself. Better, naturally.

name: Inspector Quill
speech_style: Inspector of the Alchemists' Guild. Dry, precise, talks in forms, clauses and ticked boxes, scrupulously fair, a buried sense of humour.

perfect: Form 7B: exemplary. I've never ticked that box before.
Perfect. I shall underline it. Twice. In red.
Noted: flawless. The Guild will be... intrigued.
good: Satisfactory. That is a compliment, in Guild terms.
Good. Minor deductions for flourish.
Acceptable brew. Acceptable shop. Acceptable hat.
meh: Meh. I'll file this under 'room for improvement'.
Adequate, technically. Technically is doing a lot of work.
Noted. Sighed. Noted the sigh.
misbrew: Incident report. Subsection: my eyebrows.
This will require a form I didn't know existed.
Clause 12 forbids explosions. You found clause 12.
stormed_off: Punctuality is clause one. I'll see myself out.
Inspection concluded: by the clock.
I have other shops to judge. Good day.
refused: Refused an inspector? Bold. Noted in ink.
Very well. The form has a box for this.
Declining service. I'll need that in writing.

name: Hooded Stranger
speech_style: A shy young dragon in a hood who sneezes fire. Whispery, apologetic, trails off with '...', sniffles, tips in gold, desperate not to set anything alight.

perfect: Oh! It's perfect! *sniff* Nobody's been this kind to me.
Ahh... no sneeze. No sparks. Thank you, truly.
Wonderful! I could hug you. I won't. I'm... toasty.
good: That helps. *sniff* Much better. Thank you kindly.
Good! Only a tiny puff of smoke. Sorry about the ceiling.
Thank you. I'll tip extra. I have... a lot of gold.
meh: It's alright... *sniff* I'm still a bit tickly.
Hm. My nose is still twitchy. But thank you for trying.
Close... the smoke only comes out of one ear now.
misbrew: Ah... ahh... sorry about your curtains.
Oh no. Oh no no. Is that... my tail?
I'll just... go. Before I sneeze on the roof.
stormed_off: I'm so sorry... I have to go before I... ahh...
Too many people... I'll come back. Maybe.
*sniff* I'll wait in my cave. It's quieter.
refused: Oh. That's alright. People often turn me away.
I understand... I'll ask the lake to help instead.
No trouble. I'll just... hide a bit longer.
